# Scenario 5: allow-ports-mapping=true keeps ports and rewrites unbound host IP
# - ports without a host IP are published on 127.0.0.1
# - ports that already name a host IP keep that IP unchanged
# Contrast: port_stripping.txt covers the default (allow=false) strip path.

# Step 1: Initialize Git repo
cd git-repo
exec git init -b main
exec git config user.email 'test@apinfra.local'
exec git config user.name 'Test Agent'
exec git add .
exec git commit -m 'feat: allow-ports-mapping opt-in'
cd ..

cp .apinfra.template .apinfra
exec sh -c 'echo "repo=file://'$WORK'/git-repo" >> .apinfra'

# Step 2: Run agent
exec apinfra
stderr 'done duration='

# Step 3: Both services are up
docker-assert-running apinfra_e2e-ports-unbound-1
docker-assert-running apinfra_e2e-ports-bound-1

# Step 4: Unbound short-form "18080:80" → loopback; explicit allowed IP stays
docker-assert-port-binding apinfra_e2e-ports-unbound-1 127.0.0.1 18080 80
docker-assert-port-binding apinfra_e2e-ports-bound-1 127.0.0.1 18081 80


# --- FILE TEMPLATES ---

-- .apinfra.template --
namespace=dev
repoBranch=main

-- git-repo/dev/settings.yml --
version: "1.0"
projects:
  - name: e2e-ports
    enabled: true
    allow-ports-mapping: true

-- git-repo/dev/e2e-ports/docker-compose.yml --
services:
  unbound:
    image: hashicorp/http-echo:latest
    command: ["-listen=:80", "-text=OK"]
    ports:
      - "18080:80" # no host IP → must become 127.0.0.1:18080
  bound:
    image: hashicorp/http-echo:latest
    command: ["-listen=:80", "-text=OK"]
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:18081:80" # explicit allowed host IP must be preserved

-- .env --
